- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently lags; add 1–2% to forecast in first 3–5 days of sentiment shift to capture momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% in next 7–10 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- In high-sentiment volatility periods (sentiment std > 0.3), model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast variance by 1–2% in short-term (1–7 day) horizon to reflect sentiment-driven noise.
